title: Long-term trends in aggressive incidents and coercive measures at the University Clinic for Psychiatry and Psychotherapy in Bielefeld: A retrospective analysis of routine data from 2005 to 2024
summary: Avoiding the use of coercion and preventing aggressive behavior is a key objective in psychiatric hospitals. Coercive measures constitute significant infringements on fundamental rights and include, for example, treatments administered against a patient’s will (coercive treatments) as well as measures that restrict a patient’s liberty, such as physical restraints and isolation. This study examines how patients’ aggressive behavior and the use of coercive measures have changed over a twenty-year period (2005–2024) at the University Clinic for Psychiatry and Psychotherapy in Bielefeld. For this purpose, existing routine data from specialized forms documenting aggressive incidents and the use of coercive measures will be analyzed. This provides an opportunity to examine potential changes within the context of previous efforts to prevent violence and coercion under routine conditions. Specifically, the study investigates the extent to which aggressive incidents and coercive measures (restraints, isolation, forced medication) have changed in terms of, for example, their number, duration, or severity.
conditions: Diagnosis-independent: All psychiatric diagnoses according to ICD-10

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of all inpatient admissions to the psychiatric clinic and all incidents of aggression and use of coercive measures recorded using standardized forms between 2005 and 2024.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
admission to a psychiatric hospital for inpatient care between 2005 and 2024
Exclusion criteria:
Incidents of aggression not involving inpatients; missing key information on intake forms needed to link incidents to inpatient admissions
